author: Staff Reports
title: Niswonger Children's Hospital unveils renovated St. Jude affiliate clinic - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff Reports ,
1 days ago JOHNSON CITY — Niswonger Children’s Hospital recently celebrated the opening of its newly renovated St. Jude Tri-Cities Affiliate Clinic, providing a more comfortable and welcoming environment for children receiving cancer treatment and their families.
The renovations were fully funded through more than $550,000 in donations from local philanthropists.
Designed to create a welcoming, child-friendly atmosphere, the redesigned clinic features a safari theme, including a waterfall feature in the hallway. Improvements also include a self-service drink and snack station, a counseling room, a music therapy room and two extra-large examination rooms designed to accommodate larger families.
“We are so appreciative of our community. This is a project that was initiated when a local philanthropist simply observed a need and asked how they could help,” said Chris Jett, chief executive officer of Niswonger Children’s Network. “Without this clinic, families would have to travel outside the region, sometimes as far as Memphis, to get the oncology care their children need. We’re incredibly grateful that families can access truly world-class care right here in Johnson City.”
Pediatric oncology and hematology services became available in the region in 1990 when East Tennessee State University’s Quillen College of Medicine established its pediatric hematology and oncology practice.
The program became a formal affiliate of St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital in 1999 and continues to provide advanced cancer care for children throughout the region.
Over the years, the program has expanded to offer comprehensive services for children with cancer, including child life services, social services, counseling and music therapy, along with other services available through Niswonger Children’s Hospital, where the clinic is located.
“This clinic has become such an important staple in the region and now serves families across the Appalachian Highlands,” said clinic director Kate Strickland. “These changes have already improved visits for our patients, who are facing some of the most uncertain and frightening times of their lives. Even just changing the décor to be more kid-friendly has made a huge difference, which means the world to our patients and their families.”
Jett credited the generosity of local donors for making the renovations possible.
“These renovations have been possible because of the generosity of our fellow community members,” Jett said. “Our region is extremely blessed to have this clinic, and we’re grateful that our donors made it possible to complete these updates and totally reimagine the experience for our patients and their support systems.”
